time_scope: Dixon 1981 lexical corpus as modeled by Hayes & Wilson
claim: The learned grammar contains weak minimal-word penalties on both the vowel and segmental projections, each with weight 0.94; Hayes & Wilson explicitly treat these as low-weight effects compatible with the rarity of very short words rather than as categorical bans.
formal_environment: phonological word with too little projected material
exceptions_or_counterexamples: Monosyllables do occur: the corpus contains 15 monosyllabic words, all heavy, less than 1% of the learning data. The authors state that speaker judgments on their aberrance are unavailable.

time_scope: Dixon 1981 lexical corpus as modeled by Hayes & Wilson
claim: Several learned CV/VC constraints involving /i, iː/ are explicitly attributed to the vowels' low baseline frequency rather than promoted as categorical phonotactics: /i, iː/ occur at about half the frequency of corresponding /u, a/ and /uː, aː/ in the learning data.

observations: sonorant+iː sequences in the learning data all come from one root ŋiːɻa 'tie up'

normalized_environment: low-frequency segment combinations receive gradient learned penalties
scope: learned grammar; not asserted as Dixon-style categorical restriction
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The authors caution that expected counts may already be explained by individual-segment frequencies and identify this as a possible constraint-selection artifact.

time_scope: Dixon 1981 lexical corpus as modeled by Hayes & Wilson
claim: Hayes & Wilson give an explicit overfitting case where the learner constructs a highly specific sequence constraint from only two roots containing a long vowel followed by /r/; both happen to continue with an unstressed short low vowel because initial heaviness prevents that vowel from receiving stress.
formal_environment: Vː r ă with following low vowel unstressed
normalized_environment: lexically induced specific sequence penalty from tiny root sample
exceptions_or_counterexamples: The source itself calls the constraint unlikely and proposes larger root corpora or segment-frequency baselines as remedies; it should not be treated as a categorical Wargamay restriction.
table_figure: prose example; related constraint listed in Appendix B
